claims.evidence: NHS stop smoking services page and Better Health: services offer NRT, nicotine-free medicines and support; people can self-refer via the NHS Better Health website.
NHS page: services provide NRT, medicines, advice and support; support usually up to about 12 weeks.
NHS page: e-cigarettes are not currently available as medicines so services cannot supply or prescribe them; local service may offer a free starter pack.
NHS Better Health: cravings last up to 15 minutes (NHS inform says typically 3 to 5 minutes); withdrawal symptoms are temporary, strongest in the first week, on average three to four weeks.
No returned text mentioned a personalised quit plan or the NHS Quit Smoking app; search budget exhausted before it could be checked.
NHS page: services give information, advice and professional support, usually up to about 12 weeks.
NHS Better Health: NRT in forms including patches and gum; nicotine-free medicines varenicline, cytisine and bupropion (Zyban).
NHS: get them through a local Stop Smoking Service or GP; self-refer via the NHS Better Health website in England.
Nothing returned said arrangements differ between the four UK nations. Only found that eligibility for starter packs varies by local area.
claims.newSentence: What a local service offers, such as eligibility for a free e-cigarette starter pack, varies by area.

claims.evidence: NHS Better Health NRT page lists patches, gum, lozenges, microtabs, mouth spray and nasal spray; inhalators were not seen in the returned text.
claims.newSentence: Nicotine replacement therapy comes as patches, gum, lozenges, microtabs, and mouth and nasal sprays.

claims.evidence: The returned NHS NRT page text did not say 'safe, proven to work, double the chances'; it said NRT gives nicotine without the harmful chemicals in cigarettes and that combining nicotine-free medicine with NRT makes people over 5 times more likely to quit. 'Safe' also breaks the site rule.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says nicotine replacement therapy gives the body nicotine without the other harmful chemicals found in cigarettes and tobacco.

claims.evidence: NHS Better Health: varenicline helps by blocking nicotine's effects in the brain. 'Makes smoking less enjoyable and helps with withdrawal symptoms' was not in the returned text.
claims.newSentence: Varenicline works by blocking the effects of nicotine in the brain.

claims.evidence: NHS Better Health nicotine-free medicines page: combining these medicines (varenicline, cytisine, bupropion) with nicotine products offers the best chance of success. Note one local formulary advises against some combinations, hence the attribution to NHS pages is right.
NHS page: e-cigarettes not currently available as medicines, so cannot be supplied by services or prescribed.
NHS page: local service may offer a free e-cigarette starter pack (eligibility varies).
NHS Better Health: pulse rate starts to return to normal after 20 minutes.
NHS Better Health Quit smoking page: carbon monoxide falls to non-smoker levels by 48 hours (nicotine cleared and taste/smell improve at 48 hours per another NHS page).

1 year: NHS Better Health says heart attack risk halves compared with a smoker. 10 years: NHS pages say the risk of lung cancer halves (NHS 111 Wales wording), not 'risk of dying from' lung cancer; the timings are correctly paired.
claims.newSentence: After one year the risk of a heart attack is about half that of a person who smokes, and after ten years the risk of lung cancer is about half.

claims.evidence: NHS mental health benefits page: once the withdrawal stage has passed, people have reduced anxiety, depression and stress.

Withdrawal being temporary is supported, but the list (feeling on edge, anxious, wanting a cigarette) was not in the returned text. NHS England says symptoms are strongest in the first week, especially the first three days, lasting on average three to four weeks.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says withdrawal symptoms are temporary, usually strongest in the first week and lasting on average three to four weeks.

claims.evidence: NHS inform: cravings should ease after the first two to three weeks. 'Most withdrawal symptoms fade by about two weeks' was not found and conflicts with the NHS figure of three to four weeks on average.
claims.newSentence: NHS inform, the Scottish NHS site, says cravings should ease after the first two to three weeks.

claims.evidence: NHS Better Health: cravings last up to 15 minutes (NHS inform gives 3 to 5 minutes as typical).
NHS guidance suggests walking, sugar-free gum or deep breathing to get through a craving.
No returned text mentioned a personalised quit plan or the NHS Quit Smoking app.

NHS England's November 2024 announcement was a rollout of varenicline (generic via Teva UK, tens of thousands a year, about one in four quit for six months with behavioural support). Cytisine was then under NICE review, not part of that rollout. Current Better Health pages do list cytisine as an option.
claims.newSentence: In November 2024 NHS England announced a rollout of varenicline, a stop smoking pill, to help tens of thousands of people a year try to quit.

claims.evidence: Better Health 'true impact' page: UK Alzheimer's Society says smoking increases dementia risk; smoking increases inflammation which can worsen joint pain. Hearing loss, vision loss and digestive problems were not seen in returned text.
claims.newSentence: The NHS Better Health site says the harm from smoking reaches beyond the lungs, including a higher risk of dementia and inflammation that can worsen joint pain.

claims.evidence: No returned text said smoking narrows arteries or strains the heart by raising blood pressure; could not confirm.
A targeted search found no NHS text giving 'more than 50 serious health conditions'.
NHS Better Health: smoking can feel calming but the relief is short-lived and feeds a cycle that worsens anxiety and depression; NHS mental health page says smoking increases anxiety and tension.
The returned text covered secondhand smoke risks to families (teens of smoking parents four times as likely to start) but not chest infections, meningitis or asthma.

notes: Search budget of 10 was used up, so the NHS Quit Smoking app and quit plan (c05, c24), the 50 conditions figure (c28), arteries and blood pressure (c27) and the children's risks (c30) were removed rather than confirmed; they may well be on the NHS pages and could be re-checked if budget allows. The 10-year lung cancer milestone was clearly seen only on an NHS 111 Wales page and in an NHS Better Health summary. A local formulary advises against combining some nicotine-free medicines with NRT, while NHS Better Health recommends combining them, so c13 stays attributed to NHS pages. NHS inform gives a 3 to 5 minute typical craving length versus up to 15 minutes on Better Health. No second-person commands or unrouted urgency statements in the ledger sentences.
